e.etymology: An Italian pet form of Maria, made with the diminutive ending -ella. Maria is the Latin form of the Hebrew name Miriam.
A variant of Margery, the medieval English form of Margaret, from Greek margarites (pearl). The spelling was shaped by the herb marjoram, and the name was revived in the late 19th century.
namesakes: Marjorie Taylor Greene (former Georgia congresswoman)
Marjorie Merriweather Post (cereal heiress who built Mar-a-Lago)
Marge Simpson (The Simpsons mother, formally Marjorie)

e.etymology: For girls, a Scottish and English form of Old French Jehane, a feminine of John. For boys, the French form of John. Both go back to Hebrew Yochanan (God is gracious).
namesakes: Jean Smart (actress in Hacks and Designing Women)
Jean Grey (telepath of the X-Men)
Jean Valjean (hero of Les Miserables)

assoc.t: jeans, the denim pants, and the jean jacket

e.etymology: From Latin viola (violet), the flower. Shakespeare gave the name to the shipwrecked heroine of Twelfth Night, and it was widely used in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
namesakes: Viola Davis (Oscar-winning actress)
Viola (heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night)

assoc.t: viola, the string instrument larger than a violin
viola, the garden flower related to pansies
Viola, the disguised heroine of Twelfth Night

e.etymology: A modern spelling of Cody, from an Irish surname, an Anglicized form of O Cuidighthigh (descendant of Cuidightheach, a byname for a helpful person).
namesakes: Kody Brown (patriarch of TLC's Sister Wives)

e.etymology: From Hebrew Eli'ezer, from El (God) and ezer (help). In the Bible it is the name of Abraham's steward and of a son of Moses. It is distinct from Eleazar, the source of Lazarus.
namesakes: Elie Wiesel (Holocaust survivor and author of Night, born Eliezer)

e.etymology: From Arabic Imran, the name the Quran gives to the father of Mary; its third chapter is called the Family of Imran. It corresponds to the biblical Amram, the father of Moses.
namesakes: Imran Khan (cricket star and former prime minister of Pakistan)

e.etymology: A recent coinage from the Greek-derived prefix neo- (new), popularized by the hero of The Matrix (1999), where it is also an anagram of One. Neo is separately a Tswana name from southern Africa meaning gift.
namesakes: Neo (Keanu Reeves's hero in The Matrix)

assoc.t: Neo, Keanu Reeves's hero in The Matrix

e.etymology: From an English and Scottish occupational surname for someone who shaped wood, bone or metal on a lathe, from Middle English turner.

assoc.t: Tina Turner, queen of rock and roll

e.etymology: From an English surname for someone who lived by a fen, from a southern dialect form of Old English fenn (marsh, bog). As a first name it is mostly American.
namesakes: Vance Joy (singer of Riptide)

assoc.t: JD Vance, US vice president

e.note: For now the name points straight at Vice President JD Vance, which some people will read as a political statement.

e.meaning: son of Brun, the brown-haired one
e.etymology: From an English surname meaning son of Brun, a medieval name and nickname meaning brown.
namesakes: Bronson Pinchot (Balki on Perfect Strangers)

assoc.t: Charles Bronson, tough-guy film star

e.etymology: A modern name used in Mexico and in Mexican American families. It begins like Maya-derived names such as Itzel and Itzamna; the meanings given for it in baby-name lists are not documented.
From the English word for clear quartz and fine cut glass, from Greek krystallos (ice). It was coined as a girls' name in the 19th century with other gem names and peaked in the US around 1982.
namesakes: Crystal Gayle (country singer of Don't It Make My Brown Eyes Blue)

assoc.t: crystal, clear cut glass or a mineral gem
crystal, street name for methamphetamine
Crystal, Louisiana hot sauce
comedian Billy Crystal

e.etymology: A respelling of Imani, the Swahili word for faith, from Arabic iman. Imani is the seventh principle of Kwanzaa, which brought it into use as an American given name.

e.meaning: beautiful, beloved of the god Ing
e.etymology: From Old Norse Ingiridr, which joins the name of the god Ing to fridr (beautiful, beloved). It has stayed in steady use across Scandinavia, including in its royal families.
namesakes: Ingrid Bergman (star of Casablanca)
Ingrid Michaelson (singer-songwriter)

assoc.t: Ingrid Bergman, star of Casablanca

e.etymology: An African American coinage popularized by the actor Mekhi Phifer in the late 1990s and 2000s.
namesakes: Mekhi Phifer (actor in 8 Mile and ER)

e.etymology: The Hebrew form of Jacob, from a verb related to akev (heel); in Genesis, Jacob is born holding his twin brother Esau's heel. Jacob, renamed Israel, is the father of the twelve tribes.
A girls' name in both Japan and Korea. The Japanese name can be written with many pairs of characters, so its meaning varies; the Korean name is also romanized Yoon-ah.
namesakes: Yuna Kim (South Korean Olympic figure skating champion)
Yuna (summoner heroine of Final Fantasy X)

assoc.t: Yuna, heroine of the video game Final Fantasy X

e.etymology: A name found in several unrelated languages, among them Amharic and Oromo, Japanese, Sanskrit and Kazakh. In the US it has been used mostly in African American families, alongside the spelling Ayanna.
From Gothic alls (all) and reiks (ruler). Alaric I, king of the Visigoths, sacked Rome in 410.
namesakes: Alaric I (Visigoth king who sacked Rome in 410)
Alaric Saltzman (teacher and vampire hunter in The Vampire Diaries)

assoc.t: Alaric Saltzman of The Vampire Diaries
Alaric, Visigoth king who sacked Rome in 410

e.etymology: The old Irish given name Rian, from ri (king) with a diminutive ending. It lies behind the surname O Riain, which became Ryan, and has been revived as a more Gaelic spelling of Ryan.
namesakes: Rian Johnson (director of Knives Out and Star Wars: The Last Jedi)

e.etymology: A modern phonetic spelling of Kai, or a short form of Kyle and Kyler. Kai has several unrelated sources, the best known being the Hawaiian word for sea.

A name with more than one source: a 19th-century coinage, perhaps built on Zoe or taken from the Italian surname of French novelist Emile Zola, and a southern African name from a Zulu and Xhosa word for calm.
namesakes: Zola Budd (barefoot South African Olympic runner)

assoc.t: Zola, wedding registry and planning website
Emile Zola, French novelist

e.etymology: Used in the US as a spelling of the Arabic name Amir (prince, commander). It is the given name of Questlove, the drummer of The Roots.
namesakes: Questlove (drummer of The Roots, born Ahmir Thompson)

e.etymology: A spelling of Maisie, a Scottish pet form of Margaret (Gaelic Mairead) with the -sie ending. Margaret comes from Greek margarites (pearl).
A spelling of Amina, which renders two Arabic names: Amina (safe, secure), the name of the Prophet Muhammad's mother, and Ameena (trustworthy, faithful), the feminine of Amin.
A respelling of Sincere, the English word for honest and genuine, from Latin sincerus (pure, sound). Sincere came into use as an American virtue name for boys around 2000.

The English form of Anna, the Greek and Latin form of Hebrew Hannah (grace). It spread in honor of Saint Anne, by tradition the mother of the Virgin Mary; Ann was the usual English spelling until the 20th century.
namesakes: Ann Richards (governor of Texas)
Ann Landers (advice columnist)
Ann Wilson (lead singer of Heart)

assoc.t: Ann Taylor, women's clothing store chain
Raggedy Ann, the classic red-haired rag doll

e.etymology: A spelling of Kylie (and sometimes Kaylee) with the -leigh ending. Kylie arose in Australia, possibly from an Aboriginal word for a boomerang, and spread through the fame of singer Kylie Minogue.
A spelling of Caspar, the name tradition gives to one of the three Magi. It is usually explained as coming from an Old Persian title meaning treasurer; Jasper and Gaspar are forms of the same name.
namesakes: Casper Van Dien (star of Starship Troopers)

assoc.t: Casper the Friendly Ghost
Casper, online mattress company
Casper, Wyoming

e.note: Most Americans think first of Casper the Friendly Ghost, and Casper is also a jab at very pale people.

e.etymology: From Hebrew Efrayim, read as fruitful. In Genesis, Ephraim is the younger son of Joseph and the ancestor of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
namesakes: Ephraim (son of Joseph and founder of an Israelite tribe)

e.etymology: From Arabic khadija, traditionally explained as a child born early. Khadija bint Khuwaylid, a merchant, was the first wife of the Prophet Muhammad and the first person to accept Islam.

assoc.t: Khadija, first wife of the prophet Muhammad
